source.title: Scaling Properties of Same-Family On-Policy Distillation
source.authors: Yun-Tai Bao; Qin-Feng Li; Guo-qing Jiang; Li-Wei Chen; Zhi-Heng Qin; Xuan-Ping Li; Wenqiang Zhang; Xu-Hong Zhang

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study extends scaling-law analysis to post-training on-policy distillation and reports held-out math accuracy prediction results. It does not test pretraining loss scaling.
record.gate_note: The paper cites pretraining scaling laws as related work but measures OPD training dynamics and held-out math accuracy, not held-out pretraining cross-entropy loss or compute-optimal pretraining allocations.
record.test_reason: The study gives a new-setting result on V6. It fits held-out math accuracy (peak gold score after on-policy distillation) as power laws in student and teacher parameter count and extrapolates to held-out largest scales. It reports no pretraining loss, compute-optimal allocation or architecture-shape results, so V1–V5 and V7 are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that joint power laws in student scale, teacher scale and teacher gold score predict peak gold score well at held-out scales, and predict transfer rate only approximately. Peak student error is nearly proportional to teacher error, and at matched score smaller teachers transfer better. They also find that bootstrapping does not beat direct transfer, off-policy distillation underperforms OPD, and an off-policy cold start harms weak-to-strong transfer. All results come from one Qwen2.5 family and math task with single seeds.
record.recipe_differences: The study fits scaling laws for post-training OPD outcomes and math accuracy, rather than measuring pretraining cross-entropy loss against parameter count, tokens, or compute.
record.method_sensitivity: Prediction depends on including teacher score with scale: the joint law improves over scale-only and score-only comparisons in aggregate validation; the intermediate-teacher test is predicted correctly in ordering only by the joint law. The study also reports differences between Vanilla-OPD and Delta-OPD.

fits_no_version.finding: Peak student accuracy rises with teacher scale only up to about the student's own scale. Small students lose accuracy under the largest teachers: the 0.5B student scores 40.8% with the 3B teacher, 39.0% with 7B and 37.7% with 14B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In distillation, student performance scales with teacher size only up to the student's own scale.

fits_no_version.finding: The transfer-rate power law does not beat a raw-affine baseline under leave-one-scale-out (.208/.126 vs .186/.117 for Vanilla-OPD). Transfer extent is roughly scale-free.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Distillation training-rate quantities do not follow a predictive power law in scale.

record.problems: Evidence is limited to one model family (Qwen2.5, 0.5B–14B), one math-reasoning mixture, and one run per configuration. The authors report no optimization-seed or prompt-bootstrap intervals; cell-bootstrap intervals measure variation across scale pairs, not seed uncertainty. The intermediate-teacher comparison is a single controlled validation.

untested.parts: All: no pretraining loss is measured.
All: no depth or width variation.
Other modalities. Whether the power law in loss carries over to fine-tuning or transfer regimes: accuracy error, not loss, is fitted, and only for on-policy distillation.
Prediction from pretraining loss. Tasks other than GSM8K/MATH. Model families other than Qwen2.5. Scales beyond 14B. Seed variance.
All for pretraining laws. The study compares functional forms only for its own distillation peak law.

missing.what: Student-only SFT accuracy law, 1−G_SFT = 0.682 N^−0.326. Refit through 7B, it underpredicts the 14B baseline by 4.0 points.
Outer-scale extrapolation of the weighted-additive peak law: 1.50/.92 RMSE on the student holdout vs .64/.21 for the multiplicative law, showing dependence on functional form.
Adding a learnable irreducible-error term puts it at zero: no evidence of a floor over 0.5B–14B.

record.verdict_notes: V6 is matched loosely: the outcome is post-distillation downstream accuracy rather than performance from pretraining. Most rows compare the study's own law variants. The rows linked to V6 are those that show predictability from model scale. The bootstrap intervals cover cross-pair variation, not seed variation.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Extrapolating pretraining-loss power laws from small runs to much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocations for a fixed pretraining compute budget.
The effect of depth, width, or architecture details on pretraining loss at fixed parameter count.
Power-law behavior in other modalities or other training regimes as specified by the version.
The study predicts held-out math accuracy after OPD, not general downstream performance from pretraining loss or pretraining scale.
Whether pretraining-loss exponents or compute-optimal allocations vary with setup, or whether the original pretraining curves depart from a single power law.

relationships.condition: Qwen2.5 0.5B–14B students after Vanilla- or Delta-OPD on GSM8K+MATH, predicting peak held-out accuracy with scale-based power laws
relationships.reason: Withholding the largest student, the joint law predicts within .55/.20 points and the scale-only law within .64/.21. Leave-one-scale-out and intermediate-teacher checks are also close (r1–r7).
relationships.display_finding: For Vanilla- and Delta-OPD respectively, largest-student prediction errors were 0.55 and 0.20 points for the joint law and 0.64 and 0.21 points for the scale-only law, with close agreement in additional scale and teacher checks.
